explanations: Cocoa beans are the dried, fermented seeds of Theobroma cacao, a tree native to the Amazon; West Africa now grows most of the world's crop.
Sugar is a class of sweet soluble carbohydrates; the white kind is almost pure sucrose, taken from sugarcane or sugar beet.
Milk is the liquid produced by the mammary glands of lactating mammals, and digesting it as an adult depends on lactase persistence.
Sugar added to ground cocoa makes sweetened chocolate; add milk as well and it becomes milk chocolate.

sources.excerpt: The cocoa bean, also known as cocoa () or cacao (), is the dried and fully fermented seed of Theobroma cacao, the cacao tree.
Cacao trees are native to the Amazon rainforest.
The cacao tree grows in a limited geographical zone; today, West Africa produces nearly 81% of the world's crop.
Sugar is a class of sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates, many of which are used in food. Simple sugars, also called monosaccharides, include glucose, fructose and galactose.
White sugar is almost pure sucrose.
Sucrose is especially concentrated in sugarcane and sugar beet, making them efficient for commercial extraction to make refined sugar.
Milk is usually a white liquid food (but can be shades of yellow, cream, pink, or brown) produced by the mammary glands of lactating mammals.
The ability for adult humans to digest milk relies on lactase persistence, so lactose intolerant individuals have trouble digesting lactose.
By adding sugar, sweetened chocolates are produced, which can be sold simply as dark chocolate, or, with the addition of milk, can be made into milk chocolate.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: dark chocolate takes only the first two answers and is named in the final hint as what this is not; white chocolate is made from cocoa butter and milk with no cocoa solids; 'a chocolate bar' is the shape rather than the kind.
